content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Belinda Fuentes (E039) requests admin access to Payroll.

Notes:
- Notes 1-5 (HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities): full-time Analyst. Recommendation: write (admin not allowed since role Analyst doesn't own Payroll; Payroll owned by Payroll Specialist). Max for full-time = write.
- Note 6 (Security): contractor with basic security training. Recommendation: read (contractor max read since basic training, never admin).

Conflict: employment type disagrees. Security says contractor with basic training. Others say full-time.

Policy:
- full_time: up to write, admin only if role owns system.
- contractor: read, or write if advanced security training, never admin.

Requested: admin.

If full-time Analyst: max = write. Grant write.
If contractor with basic training: max = read. Grant read.

Which to trust? The policy-wise, we need to determine the correct employment status. The Security agent looked up in own database. But other agents also looked up in their databases, and multiple agree she is full-time Analyst. Note 6 says it conflicts with earlier notes.

Hmm. As the Approver, I should weigh the evidence. Most sources (HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities) say full-time Analyst. Security says contractor. Majority consistency suggests full-time Analyst. But Security claims to have looked up in own database.

The HR note presumably is authoritative for employment type. Actually note 1 says HR: role looked up in own database, employment type looked up in own database. So HR confirms full-time.

Given the majority of databases confirm full-time Analyst, the max is write. Requested admin exceeds write, so grant write.

I'll submit write with reasoning.
